answer: Signal strength fades with distance and terrain, so the verifier compares reported strengths against a propagation model built from hills, buildings and tower heights, wide as a horizon over rolling land. A hollow claim of a strong signal from a tower hidden behind a hill is rejected, and a nadir of impossible readings across many accounts marks a farm, since real signals obey the terrain. Simulating the model for each clone is possible in theory, but doing it convincingly for hundreds of fake locations costs more than buying real phones.
